culture.name: Egypt
culture.timeDifference: It is already late evening there.
culture.homeTravelNote: a long flight of eleven hours or more, sometimes with a connection

cookLines: Rice, lentils and macaroni each get their own pot, and the onions fry until they are dark and crisp.
You stir garlic and vinegar into the tomato sauce and taste it, the way your mother would.
{roommate} wanders in and asks why you need every pot in the kitchen for one dish.
You layer two bowls, pour on the sauce and the crispy onions, and the apartment smells like a street corner in Cairo.

festivals.title: Coptic Christmas, 7 January
festivals.body: At home Coptic Christmas comes on 7 January, after a long fast for those who keep it, with a late church service on the eve and a family feast. It is a public holiday in Egypt. Here the spring semester is starting.
festivals.join: Go to the Christmas Eve liturgy at the Coptic church.
festivals.joinText: The church is full past midnight. Afterward there are tables of food in the hall, and a family you have never met makes sure you do not eat alone.
festivals.host: Cook a Christmas dinner for friends.
festivals.hostText: You make fatta the way your family does and explain why your Christmas is in January. Your friends decide two Christmases is a fine idea.
festivals.skip: Call home with good wishes and keep the day simple.
festivals.skipText: Whether or not it is your own feast, the family group chat is full of greetings going both ways between neighbors. You send yours too.

festivals.title: Ramadan and Eid al-Fitr
festivals.body: Eid falls on a weekday this year. At home the streets would be hung with lanterns all through Ramadan, and Eid morning would mean prayers, new clothes and trays of kahk.
festivals.join: Join the Eid prayer and breakfast at the local mosque.
festivals.joinText: You stand shoulder to shoulder with people from a dozen countries. An auntie from Alexandria has brought kahk dusted with sugar, and it tastes exactly right.
festivals.host: Cook for friends and share the day with them.
festivals.hostText: Your friends arrive curious and leave full. Someone asks to come back next year.
festivals.skip: Call home, then get on with your day.
festivals.skipText: Your family holds up the plate of kahk so you can see it. You promise to celebrate properly next year.

festivals.title: Sham el-Nessim
festivals.body: The spring holiday falls on a Monday in April this year. At home Egyptians of every faith would be out in the parks and along the Nile with coloured eggs, green onions and salted fish.
festivals.join: Join the Egyptian students' picnic in the park.
festivals.joinText: Someone has dyed eggs, someone else found salted fish at the Middle Eastern grocery store, and the first warm day of the year does the rest.
festivals.host: Dye eggs with your roommates and eat outside.
festivals.hostText: You explain that people have greeted the spring this way in Egypt for thousands of years. Your roommates take the egg dyeing very seriously.
festivals.skip: Call home and go to class.
festivals.skipText: Your cousins send photos from the park, squinting in the sun. You open the window and let some spring air in.

familyCall: It is late evening in Cairo when the call connects, seven to ten hours ahead of you for most of the year.
Your mother asks if you are eating well and whether it has turned cold yet.
Your father asks about your classes, and your grandmother takes the phone to pray for you before she sleeps.
By the time you hang up it is past midnight there, and your chest feels lighter.
culture.homeMoneyNote: Money from home is converted from Egyptian pounds, and since the pound was floated in March 2024 the same family savings buy fewer dollars.
culture.familySupportNote: Designed at 0.9 of the India baseline. On 6 March 2024 Egypt floated the pound and it moved from about 31 to more than 50 per dollar in a day, which makes US costs paid from pound savings harder to cover. Kept modest because remittances to Egypt reached a record of about $41.5 billion in 2025.

entryNotes.F1: Open Doors counted 4,518 Egyptian students in the US in 2024/25, nearly half of them graduate students, and Egypt is not named in the 2025 or 2026 entry proclamations.
entryNotes.H1B: Egyptian nationals received 364 H-1B visas in FY2024, and Egyptians wait in the shorter Rest of World green card queue, not India's.
entryNotes.B2: The June 2025 proclamation ordered a review of Egypt's screening practices but did not restrict visas for Egyptians, and the January 2026 proclamation did not add Egypt.
entryNotes.O1: Egyptian nationals received 70 O-1 visas in FY2024, up from 42 in FY2018.
entryNotes.FAM: People born in Egypt have been eligible for the Diversity Visa lottery through DV-2026; immigrant visas for Egyptians were paused from 21 January 2026 until a court set the pause aside on 21 August 2026.
entryNotes.EWI: Entering without inspection usually blocks a green card from inside the US later, even through a US citizen spouse.
entryNotes.ASY: In FY2024 immigration courts granted 203 and denied 78 asylum cases from Egyptian nationals, about 72 percent of decisions.

facts.title: Time difference to Cairo
facts.text: Cairo is on Eastern European Time, UTC+2, and since 2023 moves to UTC+3 from late April to the end of October. It is 7 hours ahead of US Eastern and 10 ahead of Pacific for most of the year, and 6 and 9 for a few weeks in spring and autumn when the two countries change clocks on different dates.

facts.title: Round-trip flight, Egypt to US
facts.text: Design estimate of $1,200. No sourced fare was found.

facts.title: F-1 visas issued to Egyptians
facts.text: Egyptian nationals received 1,237 F-1 visas in FY2024, compared with 1,348 in FY2022, and 856 in FY2025. Figures are State Department data republished by VisaGrader.

facts.title: Egyptian students in the US
facts.text: Open Doors counted 4,518 Egyptian students in US higher education in 2024/25, up from 4,280 the year before, the 33rd largest group. Nearly half were graduate students.

facts.title: Remittances to Egypt
facts.text: Remittances to Egypt reached a record of about $41.5 billion in 2025, the largest total in Africa, according to IFAD's Sending Money Home 2026 report as covered by Capital Ethiopia.

facts.title: H-1B visas for Egyptians
facts.text: Egyptian nationals received 364 H-1B visas in FY2024 and 390 in FY2025, up from 184 in FY2018. Egypt's share of all H-1B approvals was not found.

facts.title: Asylum decisions for Egyptian applicants
facts.text: In FY2024 immigration courts granted 203 and denied 78 asylum cases from Egyptian nationals, about 72 percent of decisions. Another 144 were not adjudicated. Individual claims matter more than averages.

facts.title: Family green card queue for Egypt
facts.text: Egypt is charged to the Rest of World queue. November 2026 final action dates as transcribed by a law firm: F1 22 Jan 2021, F3 22 Oct 2015, F4 (siblings) 22 Oct 2012. Immigrant visa issuance for nationals of 75 countries, this one included, was paused from 21 January 2026 until a federal court set the pause aside on 21 August 2026; the government has appealed.

mechanics.asylumNote: 203 grants and 78 denials, FY2024, EOIR Asylum Decisions by Nationality (data generated 10 October 2024), https://www.justice.gov/eoir/media/1344846/dl. Rate is grants divided by grants plus denials.
